profile.reading:
This is the Centrum Technologii ICM UW, the technology centre of the Interdisciplinary Centre for Mathematical and Computational Modelling at the University of Warsaw, at Kupiecka 32 in the Zeran Wschodni area of the Bialoleka district in northern Warsaw, postcode 03-046. The OpenStreetMap object carries the contact address ocean.icm.edu.pl, which is the identifying detail that ties the building to a specific machine room. ICM describes its Okeanos supercomputer, together with its analytics systems and data storage, as the main component of the OCEAN Competence Centre established in its new data centre in Warsaw at Bialoleka. This building is that data centre.

ICM was founded in 1993 by decision of the University of Warsaw Senate, growing out of the university's role in early Polish internet history, which included handling the country's first electronic mail traffic, its EARN and BITNET academic network links, the WARMAN network, and one of Poland's experimental IPv6 nodes. Its first supercomputer, a Cray EL98, arrived in 1994. Today ICM provides high performance computing to researchers and to commercial customers, runs the meteo.pl numerical weather forecasting service, built and ran the national epidemiological model for Poland during the COVID-19 pandemic, has organised the Supercomputing Frontiers Europe conference since 2018, and teaches a master's programme in computational engineering.

Because ICM is publicly funded it documents its machines in detail. Okeanos, in service since July 2016, is a Cray XC40 with 1,084 compute nodes, each holding two twelve core Intel Xeon E5-2690 v3 Haswell processors and 128 gigabytes of memory, connected by the Cray Aries interconnect in a Dragonfly topology, running SUSE Linux Enterprise Server with the Slurm scheduler over a Lustre file system. Topola is a Huawei E9000 cluster of 223 nodes at 28 cores each with 64 or 128 gigabytes of memory, and forms part of the Polish national PL-Grid research computing infrastructure. Rysy is the accelerated system, with six nodes carrying four NVIDIA V100 32 gigabyte cards apiece, one 48 core node with 1.5 terabytes of memory and eight V100 16 gigabyte cards, and one Haswell node with eight NVIDIA Titan X Pascal cards. A further partition named PBaran is a NEC SX-Aurora Tsubasa A300-8 vector machine. Users reach all of it through a single access node.

One detail from ICM's own user documentation matters for a facility registry. ICM tells its users that the server rooms holding Topola, Okeanos and Rysy are located in two different buildings, and advises them to choose storage paths accordingly to keep disk traffic local. The Kupiecka site is therefore one machine room in a multi building estate, not the whole of ICM's computing footprint.

As an academic institution ICM publishes machine specifications rather than facility specifications. No IT load, utility power service rating, standby generation capacity, on-site generation or technical floor area figure is published for this building, and none is recorded here.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05. Two problems fixed. First, the prior public text narrated this registry own failed fetch attempts (WebFetch blocked by bot detection, could not be reconfirmed this session), which does not belong in reader-facing prose and is removed. Second, Wikipedia was dropped from sources per registry policy. The main site icm.edu.pl and ocean.icm.edu.pl remain behind an Anubis proof-of-work bot wall, but ICM own HPC documentation site kdm.icm.edu.pl serves plain HTML and was fetched successfully this session, supplying all machine specifications now cited. Key new finding, the ICM computer systems page states that Okeanos with its analytics and storage systems is the main component of the OCEAN Competence Centre established in the new ICM Data Centre in Warsaw at Bialoleka, which matches the OSM contact:website tag ocean.icm.edu.pl and the Nominatim placement of way/304647589 at Kupiecka 32, Zeran Wschodni, Bialoleka, 03-046 Warszawa. This ties the building to a named facility for the first time. Also newly recorded, ICM storage documentation states the server rooms for Topola, Okeanos and Rysy sit in two different buildings, so this row is one machine room rather than all of ICM. Founding date 1993 by University of Warsaw Senate decision and the early Polish internet history retained from PIONIER coverage. No power or floor area figure is published by ICM and none is asserted.
